A dweller of Paradise asks Allah to let him farm, and his crop grows mountain-high in a wink; a bedouin says he must be from Quraysh or the Ansar.
Paradise has a hundred grades for fighters and a house of martyrs; a morning or evening in Allah's cause outweighs the world, and martyrs wish to be killed again.
Allah wonders at people who will enter Paradise in chains.
The Prophet dreams of Umar's palace in Paradise; its tents are hollow pearls, its joys beyond imagining, its first entrants shine like the full moon, and Sa'd's handkerchiefs surpass silk.
A lash's space in Paradise outweighs the world; one tree's shade outlasts a century's ride; it has lofty mansions, a wet-nurse for Ibrahim, and Ar-Raiyan gate for the fasting.
Allah has prepared for His pious servants what no eye has seen, no ear heard and no one imagined, as the verse on joy kept hidden for them says.
Paradise has two gardens of silver and two of gold, a hollow-pearl pavilion sixty miles wide, and a tree whose shade a rider cannot cross in a hundred years.
Al-Kauthar is a river the Prophet saw when taken up to the heavens, with banks of hollow-pearl tents and countless vessels; Ibn Abbas calls it the good Allah gave him.
Seventy thousand of the Prophet's followers will enter Paradise without accounts, faces shining like the moon; Ukasha, lifting his sheet, asked to be among them and was prayed for.
Seventy thousand of the Prophet's followers, faces like the full moon, will enter Paradise without reckoning, shunning branding, ruqya and omens and trusting their Lord; Ukasha asked to join them.
Allah will grant the people of Paradise His lasting pleasure, and the Prophet told Haritha's mother, her son martyred at Badr, there are many Paradises and he is in Firdaus.
A rider cannot cross a Paradise tree's shade in a hundred years; seventy or seven hundred thousand enter together, faces like the full moon, seeing its lofty abodes like stars.
Haritha, martyred at Badr, is in Firdaus, the highest of many Paradises; a journey in Allah's Cause or a foot's space in Paradise outweighs the whole world.
The Prophet asked whether his companions would be pleased to be a quarter, then a third, of the people of Paradise, and swore he hoped they would be half.
Allah will admit to Paradise whoever believes, prays and fasts Ramadan; it has a hundred degrees for those in jihad, and Firdaus, its highest, lies beneath the Beneficent's Throne.
Allah said He has prepared for His righteous slaves what no eye has seen, no ear heard and no heart imagined.
Allah will grant the people of Paradise His lasting pleasure, and a man there who wishes to farm will see his crop grow and be harvested in moments, mountain-high.
